title: Distributed Key-Value Store
question: Design a distributed, highly available Key-Value store similar to Amazon DynamoDB or Cassandra. How do you handle partitioning, replication, and consistency?

rubric.name: requirements_cap_tradeoff
rubric.description: Establishes data size, latency SLA, and explicitly chooses AP (eventual consistency) or CP system based on CAP theorem.

rubric.name: partitioning_hashing
rubric.description: Uses Consistent Hashing with virtual nodes to distribute key space evenly and enable easy node additions/removals.

rubric.name: replication_consistency
rubric.description: Configures configurable Quorum (N, R, W) where `R + W > N` for strong consistency or `R + W <= N` for eventual consistency.

rubric.name: conflict_resolution
rubric.description: Uses Vector Clocks / Version Trees or Last-Write-Wins (LWW) for concurrent update conflict resolution.

rubric.name: failure_handling_storage
rubric.description: Handles node failure via Sloppy Quorum + Hinted Handoff, Read Repair, and LSM-tree (SSTables) for fast disk writes.

expected_signals: Explains Consistent Hashing with virtual nodes to prevent hot spots
Uses Configurable Quorum (N, R, W) to tune read/write consistency
Explains LSM-tree (MemTable + WAL + SSTable) for high write performance
red_flags: Uses modulo hashing `hash(key) % N` causing massive data reshuffling on server changes
Ignores network partitions or assumes instant global synchronization
Fails to explain conflict resolution when concurrent writes occur
follow_up_prompts: What is the impact on read latency if you set Read Quorum R=1 vs R=3 in a 3-replica cluster?
How does a Gossip protocol assist nodes in discovering cluster membership changes?
